node-1.label: A 3-year-old boy has widespread warty eruptions covering the body, including the genital area, but sparing the scalp, face, palms, and soles

node-2.label: The patient is a 3-year-old boy, the only child of non-consanguineous parents, with no significant family history; otherwise in good health with no developmental delays or visual or hearing difficulties

node-3.label: Skin changes began at 3 weeks of age, initially appearing symmetrically on the anterior thighs, then spreading to the axillae, and over approximately 6 months progressed to the current widespread distribution; there was no history of blisters or generalized redness at or after birth

node-4.label: The condition improved during summer and worsened in winter

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed multiple, bilaterally symmetrical, verrucous plaques following the lines of Blaschko, extensively involving the trunk and extremities; the plaques were oriented transversely on the trunk and longitudinally on the limbs; hair, nails, and oral cavity appeared normal; systemic examination showed no abnormalities

attrs.why: Blaschko-linear verrucous plaques classic; sporadic healthy child; infantile onset without blisters; winter worsening.
Blaschko-linear verrucous supports; but male, no neonatal blisters, no extracutaneous, no seasonality refute.
Winter worsening and Blaschko verrucous support; absence of neonatal blisters/redness refutes.

node-1.label: A 3-year-old boy has widespread warty eruptions covering the body, including the genital area, but sparing the scalp, face, palms, and soles

node-2.label: The patient is a 3-year-old boy, the only child of non-consanguineous parents, with no significant family history; otherwise in good health with no developmental delays or visual or hearing difficulties

node-3.label: Skin changes began at 3 weeks of age, initially appearing symmetrically on the anterior thighs, then spreading to the axillae, and over approximately 6 months progressed to the current widespread distribution; there was no history of blisters or generalized redness at or after birth

node-4.label: The condition improved during summer and worsened in winter

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed multiple, bilaterally symmetrical, verrucous plaques following the lines of Blaschko, extensively involving the trunk and extremities; the plaques were oriented transversely on the trunk and longitudinally on the limbs; hair, nails, and oral cavity appeared normal; systemic examination showed no abnormalities

attrs.why: The pathologist's analysis of the skin biopsy (hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis with focal epidermolytic hyperkeratosis) corroborates the clinical Blaschko-linear verrucous plaques, infantile onset without blisters, and winter worsening, further strengthening systematized epidermal nevus over the alternative entities. Confidence is raised from 0.75 to 0.85; definitive molecular testing (FGFR3/PIK3CA/RAS) and imaging remain unavailable.

Winter worsening and Blaschko verrucous support; absence of neonatal blisters/redness refutes.

node-9.label: Skin biopsy shows hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis with focal epidermolytic hyperkeratosis

node-10.label: Molecular testing for FGFR3/PIK3CA/RAS mutations and brain MRI/skeletal survey are unavailable

node-11.label: Epidermal nevus syndrome (systematized epidermal nevus with possible extracutaneous involvement)

attrs.why: The pathologist notes that epidermal nevus syndrome cannot be fully excluded given the widespread Blaschko-linear verrucous plaques. However, the systemic examination is normal and brain MRI and skeletal survey are unavailable, so no extracutaneous involvement is documented, keeping this possibility low and subordinate to the leading diagnosis of systematized epidermal nevus.
